The 3rd world ruined X algorithms & payouts have rewarded the lowest quality content from the laziest "creators" sharing the same clips w/ no added context

The more you try to create original content, the less you see growth, financial incentives, & often can't find your audience that already follows you

Social media used to be about expressing authenticity & that's why people loved it. The public followed you to hear your genuine thoughts & understand how you came to those conclusions. Every niche was available. 

One day you could give a rant on the Iran War and the next moment you could be playing piano. It was never about the money or clout. YouTube's own motto used to be "express yourself"

But then the money started flowing, the followers started rising, advertisers & governments demanded censorship to remain "brand safe" and greedy people saw the opportunity to produce content like they were a machine instead of a human being. 

Corporations soon followed to control the "talent" and now our online experience is a curated algorithm intended to lower our IQs and keep us consuming low quality content that fries our dopamine receptors. 

But it seems people are picking up on the scam. The 3rd world came on the coat tails, feeding us AI fruit videos and AI voice over movie clips - as a result the consumers are checking out.

What was meant to be an answer to challenging the MSM & providing personalized content Hollywood refused to deliver ended up becoming the new mainstream slop factory. "Creators" are now just actors putting on a show & it's clear the public understands what happened, rejecting the current content & instead going back to the movies, watching Apple TV & focusing on health / wellness in the real world.

At least with Hollywood you know what you're consuming is fake, there's no LARPING trad wives or bald red pill gurus giving you pointless advice that clouds your mind with black pills & fantasies of life you'll never live. 

But something is changing in all the authentic producers of online content still lurking in the shadows of the broken code poisoning boomers on Facebook & impressionable minds on TikTok. 

They're realizing that re-hashing the same Fox News clips on X or following the same dance trends on Instagram are neither fulfilling personally nor adds anything meaningful to the world 

The desire to hear real people, genuine opinions, and explore interests outside of politics, gossip, & nothingness seems to be brewing in the masses. I'm not sure where this industry is going, but I'll never give into the temptation to sellout and stop being a real, openly flawed, complex human being.

We are so online and attached to this toxic simulation we often forget to remain grounded. The fix to this is focusing less on the conversations the algo is pushing, stop comparing yourself to people who are faking their day to day, and start becoming a better version of yourself, whether you're posting content online or not. 

Privacy is a thing of the past with Flock cameras, data centers, & self driving cars with AI cameras built into the cabins. But one thing we've lost and need to gain back, is improving our genuine selves for the sake of finding peace and aligning with God's plan for our lives.

No audience needed. The world isn't worth trying to please. The social media algorithms aren't our God. A virtual rebirth is upon us. Don't miss out by staying black pilled. Instead of likes, followers, & constant breaking news - pursue spiritual wholeness, physical wellness, quality relationships IRL, & explore the things that drive creativity, help you express your heart, and are the pillars of Western Civilization.

The next renaissance isn't in a great hall or public square, it's inside your heart, soul and mind. So I'm just going to continue posting online who I am in the real world. Take it or leave it. Life is better lived free from corporate control, financial handcuffs & to please people you've never met that will never accept the real you. Spontaneous song writing is one of my favorite things to do every day in between tasks, going to share more of it because the news cycle takes more from us than it gives. Music is healing. Find what you love to do and share it with the world so content gets back to what it was intended to do, connect & unite us in our isolated little lives.

Elon Musk (Super) Created a New ChatGPT

I changed my mind about Grok in the most expensive and coolest way possible, through Grok Bot.

I paid an extra $100 for the subscription so I could try their new product, an autonomous agent. I had just been building Pi, and I’ve been using Hermes for a long time already.

And you know what’s cool? 

When the Grok Build agent creates an app for itself so Grok Bot can run on Linux.

Within five minutes, I had a working window on my machine and opened my Meet Grok Bot. In other words, I had already started building my own personal agent.

Then I started giving it its first audits while I was still going through the Grok Bot onboarding and learning how it worked.

Grok went online with no instructions or skills, found all the relevant bug reports and references on its own, and fixed the issues.

That surprised me. Their starter harness understood the full chain of actions needed for a fix. It sounds obvious, but many agents, including Claude, are too overconfident and too lazy.

What disappointed me, though, was how much the subscription tier affects the model’s reasoning. The demo behind the Twitter checkmark, without a Super subscription, didn’t even understand its own browser use.

But everyone does this kind of “manipulation,” so I’m not going to take karma away from the authors. That’s not the important part.

What matters is that, in the best ChatGPT tradition, computer use is applied immediately. The agent looks at the app, analyzes it, and tests hypotheses.

Then I had a wild experience. After getting the initial context, including the apps I need, the agent started a conversation with me on its own. They configured the agent to be proactive.

It immediately asks questions and runs a short interview to bring you up to speed. I don’t personally need that, but it might be the best onboarding into working with agents that I’ve seen.

I was genuinely shocked when I realized I could see the virtual desktop the agent sees on the right, and throw routines and recurring tasks straight onto it.

The whole design is built to take control away from you, so everything gets handled by itself. That’s the meta in AI right now. Every top model is being designed around this exact idea.

I’m still a control freak, though. But I understand why this approach will feel absolutely insane to most people.

On the other hand, I can organize work across branches, chats, and agents. That also makes sense to me and feels familiar, but I have to give them credit for the minimalist design. I absolutely love that.

So overall, my impression is extremely positive. If you haven’t used AI before and you’re ready to spend hundreds of dollars, this is for you.

What I really, really loved about this workflow is that you just keep messaging the agent. It sees the message and immediately picks it up as work.

The lack of commands and buttons makes me a little uneasy, but that’s the whole philosophy: work without stopping.

For everyone else, it’s too expensive. But it’s beautiful.

And most importantly, this is a full autonomous agent. No need to install your own server or rent more powerful hardware.

Then I asked it to understand my workflow, find all of my agent settings and tools, and go make a video. I deliberately gave it a task where it has to figure everything out and do the work itself.

MEET THE AI GIRL WHO PLAYS TENNIS FOR A LIVING — AND SHE'S NEVER LOST

She trains, competes, and racks up wins on camera. The catch: she doesn't exist.

Here's how the "AI athlete" model actually works:

An AI girl persona is built with a consistent face, body, and personality using image/video generation tools. Instead of lifestyle or fashion content, her niche is sport — match highlights, training vlogs, "behind the scenes" prep, rackets and outfits, rivalries with other AI athletes.

The mechanism is simple: physical talent doesn't need to be real, only the narrative around it does. Generated match clips, fake tournament brackets, and AI commentary create a storyline fans follow like a real career.

How she earns:

Sponsorship deals with sportswear/equipment brands looking for cheap, controllable "athletes"
Paid fan subscriptions for exclusive training content and match reactions
Licensing her face/likeness to sports betting or fantasy-sim apps
Selling a personal "AI coach" app trained on her persona
NFT/collectible drops tied to her "career milestones" (Grand Slam wins, rankings)

The twist: her fanbase doesn't care that she's never held a racket — they're not following an athlete, they're following a story that updates on schedule
